subject.title: feat: contextual group activation — LLM-driven peeking/engaged state machine

question: Should OpenClaw support LLM-driven contextual activation for unmentioned group traffic, and should it live in shared core activation, channel/plugin APIs, or a narrower attention/ambient-room feature?
rationale: Automation can show the current gap, but maintainers must choose the privacy, consent, provider-exposure, retention/logging, config, and ownership contract for processing unmentioned group traffic.

options.title: Sponsor default-off design first
options.body: Approve a maintainer-owned design with explicit consent, provider exposure, retention/logging, config schema, channel coverage, and tests before accepting code.

options.title: Narrow to attention behavior
options.body: Pursue timer-based attention windows or ambient room-event ergonomics without adding a model-driven background peeking path yet.

options.title: Move to plugin/API seam
options.body: Design the observation and decision-hook APIs needed to keep this optional policy outside core runtime defaults.

recommendation.title: Sponsor default-off design first
recommendation.body: Approve a maintainer-owned design with explicit consent, provider exposure, retention/logging, config schema, channel coverage, and tests before accepting code.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across the central activation and mention-policy code paths that this decision would extend.
